lines.trans: All of you ladies are professionals, aren't you?
Still, can we really pull off a strip show that suddenly?
You can! You ladies can do anything. Naturally, it may not go smoothly at first.

words.gloss: be known (in かもしれない)

lines.trans: In short, this serves as live promotion for every one of you.
Are we actually getting paid for this?
Of course you'll get paid—plenty! Your fan base will definitely grow.
Then video sales will double, and your pay will double right along with them.
Let's do it—let's put on a strip show!
Mr. Muranishi told me I didn't have to go.
Won't it be rough ahead if you isolate yourself? Ms. Kuroki worked alongside everyone and was loved for it.

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: Ms. Kuroki and I are different.
Then all the more reason you ought to go join them, don't you think? Have a good show.

meanings.note: Polite way to address a group of people.

examples.text: 皆さんにお知らせがあります。
examples.trans: I have an announcement for everyone.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: プロの女優として、監督であるあなたの注文には応えるって。
examples.trans: She says as a professional actress, she'll meet your requests as director.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Polite presumptive form of copula だ; with rising intonation, seeks agreement.

examples.text: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
examples.trans: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 急 (sudden).

examples.trans: Calling me by my bare name all of a sudden, huh?

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Confident everyday word that works either before a predicate or as a standalone answer.

examples.text: もちろん手伝いますよ。
日本一の映画監督、初のハリウッド作品。
examples.trans: Japan's number-one film director, making his big American debut.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: つまりこれはね、皆さんにとってプロモーションなんですよ。
examples.trans: In short, this serves as live promotion for every one of you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
I-adjective; 多くて means 'at most'.

examples.text: 今日は人が多いですね。
examples.trans: There are a lot of people today.

examples.text: もちろん出る、多く出る。確実にファンが増える。
examples.trans: Of course you'll get paid—plenty! Your fan base will definitely grow.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Intransitive ichidan verb meaning something increases in number or amount.

examples.text: 最近お客さんが増えました。
仕事が増えて忙しくなりました。
examples.trans: Work increased and I got busy.

examples.text: そしたら売り上げが倍増する、ギャラも倍増するわけですよ。
examples.trans: Then video sales will double, and your pay will double right along with them.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

examples.text: やりましょう、ストリップを！
examples.trans: Let's do it—let's put on a strip show!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: 孤立したらこの先つらいんじゃない？黒木さんはうまくやって慕われてたんだから。
examples.trans: Won't it be rough ahead if you isolate yourself? Ms. Kuroki worked alongside everyone and was loved for it.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: 孤立したらこの先つらいんじゃない？黒木さんはうまくやって慕われてたんだから。
examples.trans: Won't it be rough ahead if you isolate yourself? Ms. Kuroki worked alongside everyone and was loved for it.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Alone as 違う！ or 違います, means 'No, that's wrong!'.
Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

いってらっしゃい.gloss: have a good day; see you later

meanings.en: have a good day; take care (said to someone leaving)
meanings.note: Standard greeting said by those staying behind when someone leaves home.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、気をつけてね。
examples.trans: Have a good day, take care.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、早く帰ってね。
examples.trans: See you later, come home early.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
